Name: HTT Japan - Grandpa's Shed
Author: Otterhead
Description:
[center][font=Verdana][size=6][b][/b][/size][/font][size=6]星の[/size][size=6]露[/size][size=6]の谷[/size]
[size=5]Hoshi no Tsuyu no Tani (HTT)
[/size][size=3] ⁂ Valley of the Dew of the Star ⁂[/size][size=3]
[/size][size=3][/size][/center][left][size=3]This is the first mod I made for HTT, changing the [i]exterior[/i] of Grandpa's Shed from SVE into a new Japan-based theme. It includes the [i]ruined shed[/i] and the [i]repaired shed[/i], as well as [i]seasonal[/i] variations for both versions and [i]inclement weather[/i] variations for the repaired shed (the ruined shed doesn't change with weather because it's, well, ruined already!)[/size]
[size=3]
If you're curious, many of my HTT mods are based off real places in Japan. HTT Grandpa's Shed design is inspired by one of the Kura, or Japanese storehouses, found in a small Japanese fishing village called Miura. The building is actually home to a really cool wine bar and cafe called [url=https://retty.me/area/PRE14/ARE40/SUB4003/100001559546/]Couronne[/url].﻿

_____

I really love [/size][size=3][url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/9704]Updated Seasonal Japanese Buildings[/url] and have used it since I started playing Stardew Valley with mods. However, it's missing buildings from some mod expansions (like SVE), some of the buildings are not coherent as an aesthetic, and there are things I want to change in general, so I've used it as inspiration going forward. There are open permissions from the original creator [/size][url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/3947][size=3]S[/size][size=3]onreirblah[/size][/url][size=3] because they are no longer working on the initial mod at all, and [url=https://next.nexusmods.com/profile/Leroymilo/about-me?gameId=1303]Leroymilo[/url] was kind enough to give permission for me to use whatever they had also added on to the mod when they updated it for 1.6.[/size][size=3]﻿[/size][/left][size=3]
[i][b]I create my visual mods digitally by hand out of a desire to share my love of Japanese architecture and aesthetics, and do not condone the use of AI in creative works like images, visual design, graphic design, etc. AI is a tool that should be used sparingly, responsibly and ethically.
[/b][/i]
_____
